title: Collision
brief: Rebuild the cross-session edit warning to the standard: it warns when two Claude Code sessions on this machine edit the same file. Known faults of the earlier version: unlocked read-modify-write of the shared file, so two sessions lose each other's entries; eviction by key order can drop a recently re-edited file as oldest; once warned, a file never warns again; relative paths are not resolved and only drive-letter paths are lowercased; MultiEdit and edits made through Bash are unseen; the warning arrives after the edit instead of at tool.check; the shared file lives in the plugin folder and is lost on reinstall; the session id falls back to Math.random; one test, with no concurrency or eviction case; it acts while switched off.

stamps.reason: 1. Off is not inert: tool.call calls $.clock.now() before the switch check, against the standard and the spec's own Off section ('the only work is the switch check'); A21 lists fs, env and session but leaves clock out. Check the switch first and add clock to A21. 2. A reachable state is not drawn: on, nothing edited here, another session seen (others >= 1 after an Edit tool.check that read the folder, or after clear). Empty and Working do not cover it, and the Working card with 0 others is not specified either (is the second line hidden?). No acceptance line proves the 'other session(s) editing nearby' line or its plural. 3. 20 columns: only the meetings card is drawn there. The note '2 shared' is cut to '2 sh…' (the card leaves about 5 characters beside the title; pick a note that fits), and the Working lines (21 and 30 characters) are not drawn or said to wrap or shorten at 16 inner columns. 4. Row state is colour alone: red, yellow and green rows have identical text, so without colour, and to anyone who has not read the spec, the card never says an edit was stopped. Give the state a word or glyph that survives at 20 columns and have A4/A10/A23 prove it. 5. Error state has no way back: say when isBlind clears (a later write that succeeds) and prove it. A19 joins two cases that differ: with no home folder dir is unknown, so nothing can be read and 'still denies from what it can read' cannot be tested for it; split the line. The card text says 'above the two lines' but draws three. 6. Slot reuse takes 'the entry in dir with the oldest mtimeMs' without limiting it to kind file and a .json name: FsEntry gives a directory mtimeMs 0, always older than 24 hours, so a stray folder becomes the slot and every write fails, and a non-.json name is never read by the other sessions. Limit it and add the edge to A17. 7. A12 as written ('two engines on one ground file map') does not match the stamped kit: ground() builds its own file map per engine and takes no shared one. Say how the test shares the map, or reword it so the second session's file is written by the test between this session's writes.
stamps.subject: spec

stamps.reason: 1. After /clear the session collides with itself. The spec says the session id changes on /clear with no session.start, and that a slot found holding another id is abandoned for <id>.json. After /clear the slot holds the old id of this same session, so the session leaves its own file behind and reads it as another session for up to 30 minutes: the card says 1 other nearby when the person is alone; a file recorded through Bash (mine set, seen not set) is denied at the next Edit as edited by another session in this very folder; and after the clear verb (seen wiped) every file edited before /clear is denied the same way, each time telling the user two sessions are at work. Right: keep the last id this session wrote in the watch state; a slot holding that id is still its own and is overwritten under the new id, and only a slot holding an id this session never wrote moves it to <id>.json. Add an acceptance line: session.id answers a new id mid-session, then an Edit of a file edited before it is not denied, others stays 0 and the folder holds one file for this session. 2. Demo stand-ins are incomplete. docs/engine.js has no fs.stat (fs is read, write, list only), and its scripted turn runs two successful Bash calls after the Edit (npm test, git commit) with no isReadOnly, so the Bash path calls a function that does not exist and the demo card errors or never reaches 1 met. Name the fs.stat stand-in and what it answers, and state that the row is still stopped after those two Bash calls (the earlier Read and the failing Bash come first; say so). 3. The Bash stat pass has two unstated edges. (a) fs.stat rejects on a missing path and nearly every word of a command (npm, test, -am) is not a file; say a rejected stat is skipped and prove it in A9 with a command that holds non-file words. (b) A word of the command that another session also holds: the spec applies the more-than-2000-after rule only to keys taken from another session, so a file the other session edits while a long command that merely names it is running (bun test a.test.ts) is recorded as changed by this command and warned about falsely. Say the rule applies to every candidate another session holds, named or not, and add that case beside A11.
stamps.subject: spec

stamps.reason: The three faults of the last review are fixed and every hook and call named exists in the types file; what remains is acceptance lines missing for edges the Data section states. 1. A tool.call whose result is an error or a deny is returned untouched and records nothing, but no line proves it. A failed Edit (old_string not found, the commonest real error) that was recorded would publish the file as edited and stop the other session falsely. Add a line: an Edit, a Write and a Bash whose result has isError true, and an Edit whose result is { deny }, each leave mine, seen and the meetings unchanged, write no file, make no fs.stat call and return the same object. 2. A Read turns a changed meeting into re-read (Data, Read), but A4 proves only stopped to re-read. Extend A10: after the changed row, a Read of the file shows the check mark and re-read, and the next Edit tool.check returns the verdict beneath. 3. Two caps have no line: at most 40 fs.stat calls per command (a command of 100 words plus other sessions' keys makes 40 stat calls, not more), and seen capped at 200 by oldest time (201 Reads keep 200, the oldest dropped, the newest kept). Add a line for each. Small, fix in passing: the Demo section lacks a full stop between 'targets' and 'The turn'.
stamps.subject: spec

stamps.reason: The three faults of the last review are fixed, the spec is within size at 104 lines and 15 acceptance lines, and no blocking fault remains; 14 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

Built collision-widget to the spec: edits are denied at tool.check when another session changed the file since this one last read it, Bash changes are found by a stat pass and warned once, each session writes only its own file under the config folder, and all 15 acceptance lines have tests.

Meets the spec and the standard, and in live runs it recorded an Edit and a Bash change and refused a real edit at tool.check ahead of core's own stale-file error; six non-blocking findings in inspection.md, the first for the clerk (demo stand-ins).
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
